assessment.nobel_worthiness: Theory prediction of flat bands at the magic angle followed by experimental demonstration of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene opened an entire field of moire quantum materials. From a first-principles materials perspective it is a striking case where band structure engineering via a single control parameter produces strongly correlated phases, and it has had very broad influence on condensed-matter research.
assessment.attribution: The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model supplied the decisive theoretical prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group delivered the decisive 2018 experiments. Eva Andrei's earlier STM evidence of flat bands is also important, and leaving her out is a genuine allocation difficulty, but three names give a coherent theory-plus-experiment configuration.
assessment.maturity: Roughly eight years since the experiments, with wide independent replication across many groups and platforms. The core phenomenology is robust, although the microscopic origin of the superconductivity is still debated.
uncertainties: Credit for early experimental evidence (Andrei and others) could complicate the three-person limit.
Whether the field is mature enough to single out one discovery rather than a family of moire effects.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators changed how band structure is classified, linking spin-orbit coupling, symmetry and topology to protected surface and edge states. The concept is foundational, has been verified in many materials, and connects directly to electronic-structure calculations that identified candidate materials.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the theoretical proposal of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 classification; Molenkamp's group observed the HgTe quantum well edge transport following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang prediction. Hasan's ARPES work on 3D topological insulators is also decisive for the three-dimensional case, and the BHZ theory credit is not within the supplied names, so the allocation is not clean.
assessment.maturity: Nearly two decades of independent confirmation across 2D and 3D materials, with a stable interpretation. Recognition could be viewed as timely or somewhat overdue given the 2016 prize on topological phase transitions.
uncertainties: Credit split between 2D and 3D discoveries and the omission of the BHZ prediction from the supplied names.
Overlap with the 2016 prize may weigh on how the committee frames novelty.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory gave the first controllable non-perturbative framework for strongly correlated electrons, capturing the Mott transition and, combined with density functional theory, a route to real correlated materials. This is conceptually original and widely used, and I know the electronic-structure applications of the method well from my own field.
assessment.attribution: Metzner and Vollhardt introduced the infinite-dimension limit; Georges and Kotliar established the mapping onto a self-consistent impurity problem. Muller-Hartmann and Jarrell also contributed, and the supplied names omit some of these, so the credit is reasonable but incomplete.
assessment.maturity: More than thirty years of use with extensive validation against experiment and numerical benchmarks. The method is an approximation whose accuracy for low-dimensional systems is limited, but its impact is extremely well established.
uncertainties: Impact is largely methodological; the committee may ask whether it counts as a discovery or invention of sufficient physical character.
Incomplete credit set given the several contributors to the original formulation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cold atoms in optical lattices realize Hubbard models with tunable parameters, giving quantum simulation of many-body phases such as the superfluid-Mott transition and now single-site resolved microscopy. The impact on how we study correlated lattice models is large and it has produced new probes unavailable in solids.
assessment.attribution: Jaksch-Zoller proposed the Bose-Hubbard realization; Greiner, Bloch and Hansch observed the Mott transition; Greiner and Bloch pioneered quantum gas microscopy. Esslinger's fermionic Mott work and Cirac's theory are also strong, so exclusion of two or more names is a real problem.
assessment.maturity: Over twenty years of results from many independent labs with consistent interpretation. Some of the grand aims of quantum simulation are still being realized, but the foundation is solid.
uncertainties: Selection among five credited names is difficult.
Overlap with earlier BEC and cooling prizes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance and coherent spin-dependent tunnelling through crystalline MgO moved spintronics into read heads and magnetic random-access memory. The physics of symmetry-filtered tunnelling is well understood from first-principles calculations, and the practical impact is huge.
assessment.attribution: Moodera and Miyazaki first reported large room-temperature TMR in amorphous barriers; Parkin and Yuasa independently demonstrated giant TMR in MgO, following theoretical predictions by Butler and by Mathon and Umerski that are not among the supplied names. Choosing three of four credited names leaves Miyazaki out.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature with decades of industrial deployment and independent confirmation. The 2007 prize for giant magnetoresistance partly overlaps in subject, which may reduce the sense of novelty.
uncertainties: Leaving out Miyazaki and the theorists of coherent tunnelling.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock with magic wavelengths delivers fractional uncertainties in the 10^-18 range and enables tests of fundamental physics and a possible redefinition of the second. It is a clear, important and original invention with lasting impact on precision measurement.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and Ye led the demonstration of the highest-performance clocks and comparisons. Two names give a clean configuration, though others contributed to the strontium and ytterbium platforms.
assessment.maturity: Many independent groups have reproduced the performance, and the redefinition of the second is under discussion. Recognition feels timely, with earlier clock-related prizes in 2005 and 2012 as context.
uncertainties: Overlap with prior prizes in frequency metrology.
Credit shared with other clock groups not in the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit quantum electrodynamics provides the architecture for superconducting qubits and strong light-matter coupling on a chip, and it underpins most current quantum processors. The work is original and the impact on quantum technology is large.
assessment.attribution: Blais and Schoelkopf, with Girvin and others, provided the theory and the 2004 experiments; Wallraff led the first strong-coupling demonstration. Girvin is not among the supplied names, which is a credit problem.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed across many laboratories, though the committee may consider the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in superconducting circuits and decide that the topic is covered for now.
uncertainties: Missing contributors such as Girvin and Devoret in the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: High-gain X-ray free-electron lasers provide ultrashort, intense coherent X-ray pulses that are transforming studies of structure, ultrafast magnetism and electronic dynamics. The importance for materials and spectroscopy is large, and I know facilities of this type as a user community perspective.
assessment.attribution: The SASE concept and high-gain theory trace to Bonifacio, Pellegrini and Narducci, Kim and others, with experimental realization at LCLS and FLASH. Since the supplied names do not include every founder, the allocation is contentious and depends on how one weights theory versus machine building.
assessment.maturity: Several facilities operate worldwide with consistent results, so maturity is good. The prize question is mainly about attribution, since the discovery is an accelerator and team achievement.
uncertainties: Large team achievements make a three-person credit assignment hard.
Whether the work is judged as physics discovery or as an instrument.
Uncertain recall of the exact historical contributions.
